newsitem.title: UK: British Biotech up after positive meeting. [CORRECTED 15:56 GMT]
newsitem.headline: British Biotech up after positive meeting. [CORRECTED 15:56 GMT]

text.p: Shares in British Biotech Plc rose on Thursday following upbeat comments by company directors to about six institutional investors yesterday at brokerage Greig Middleton, analysts and traders said.
(Corrects from "... an upbeat presentation by finance director James Noble").

A spokeswoman for British Biotech said Noble's comments focused on the company's product marketing plans but stressed it was just the latest in a series of presentations to institutional investors in recent months.
The stock was up 16p at 218-1/2 by 1406 GMT.
Volume was a moderate 1.5 million shares.
The stock has languished in recent weeks after climbing as high as 377p during May amid a wave of speculation about prospects for key drugs such as cancer treatment Marimastat.

Yet the stock dropped back from its May highs as investor interest in the biotech sector waned and British Biotech's 143 million stg rights issue was taken up by only 49 percent of its shareholders -- leaving the majority with underwriters.
The spokeswoman said the company had been responding to requests for briefings from a large number of institutional investors.
"We have had a lot of institutions approaching us, there is a lot of interest in the company," she said.
Analysts pointed out that British Biotech was due to make two potentially significant announcements in November.

On November 4 it is due to issue a release on research progress with Marimastat, timed to coincide with a Vienna conference of the European Society for Medical Oncology, which will hear five presentations on the drug.
On November 27 it is due to report first-half results, including UK phase III results of acute pancreatitis product Lexipafant.
